title: Decode exact represented qLTC syndromes without a minimum-weight oracle
statement: Given the actual fixed-code combinatorial representation and clean syndrome, local finite-search descent plus inverse-transpose kernel lifting corrects every Pauli error of weight<=rho_star N, rho_star=2^(-2^21). One may take L_Z=12 s0 D0^5, L_X=24 s0 T0 D0^4, T0=2^49 D0^20. The supplied fixed specialization bounds 1+L_X+L_Z<2^786652 and code distance>=2^-262144 N. The corrected residual has zero syndrome and weight below code distance, hence is a stabilizer. Genuine channels with Kraus operators in the promised low-weight Pauli span are corrected on arbitrary encoded/reference-entangled inputs. Sorted-record finite-BIT work is O(C_loc N^2 log^2(2N)); no noisy-syndrome or adversarial recovery claim.

It provides a reference-safe energy-to-correctable-subspace tail/trace-distance bound, a conditional operator gap-transfer lemma, and transport of the storage inequality under bounded-depth physical unitary changes. The full constant-locality/dimension, constant normalized energy-gap quantum-PCP compiler remains OPEN; neither a full compiler nor an unrestricted obstruction is obtained.
review.source_availability: No construction of a robust local computation test satisfying P_r B P_r>=beta P_r on every physical NO-state; no complete charged arithmetic-tower construction from an arbitrary QMA instance. Clean syndrome decoding is not noisy-syndrome handling, adversarial fault-tolerant computation or a local coherent verification relation. Reference-safe correction is warranted for genuine error channels with Kraus operators in the low-weight Pauli span; decoding an arbitrary low-distance vector does not identify a prior intended logical state. Logical changes inside the codespace have zero code energy, so code energy does not impose initialization, propagation or rejection. The adversarial-computation guarantee f(N)=2^-O(sqrt(log N)) remains vanishing, includes its noiseless classical-function/logical-postselection qualifications, and supplies no proved circuit-to-Hamiltonian correspondence. Average code energy e over L frames gives only Pr(any bad frame)<=Le/g; a constant per-time fault guarantee is not established.
